initial_observation.demographics: A female child in her adolescence
initial_observation.encounter_context: presented with swelling on the left upper back over the scapular region
initial_observation.chief_complaint: swelling on the left upper back over the scapular region for the past 4 years
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The swelling was noticed insidiously and was gradually increasing in size, not associated with pain, no loss of function or history of any neurological deficit. There was no history of previous trauma.
presenting_symptoms: swelling on the left upper back over the scapular region

evidence_items.source_text: On clinical examination, a single swelling measuring about 12×11 cm was observed over the left scapular region extending 6 cm below the head of humerus superiorly, medially extending up to the midline, laterally up to the posterior axillary line, and inferiorly up to the seventh intercostal space. The swelling was firm in consistency and non-tender, had smooth overlying surface and was immobile. Distal pulse and neurological examination of the left upper extremity were normal.
Plain radiograph of the right chest revealed normal study.

MRI of the left scapula revealed a hyperintense lesion (12×1.7×12 cm) on the left paravertebral region extending from D5 to D12, which is suppressed on STIR sequence (figure 1). The lesion was also extending into the fifth intervening intercostal space, causing its widening due to mass effect. Visualised vertebral bodies showed normal signal intensity and morphology. The final impression of MRI was lipoma.
Tru-cut biopsy was performed which was suggestive of lipoma.
Histopathology of the excised specimen was given as lipoma.

The patient underwent complete surgical excision. The mass was excised from the surrounding soft tissues and underlying periosteum to which it was densely adhered. The fifth intercostal space was widened and the mass was seen entering into the intercostal space but the pleura was not breached (figure 2).

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: Histopathology of the excised specimen was given as lipoma.
